reasoning_log_text: The study analyzed MaDeLaNe data across species and cortical layers, revealing that global oddball responses were restricted to higher-order areas (e.g., PFC in monkeys, late visual cortex in mice), contradicting feedforward error propagation hypotheses. Local oddballs showed widespread activity early in the hierarchy but did not support predictive suppression mechanisms like synaptic depression or inhibition via SST/PV interneurons for GO contexts. Granger causality and laminar analysis indicated feedback dominance over feedforward processing during global oddball stimuli, challenging H2 hypotheses. Ubiquity factors (H3) were partially supported for LO but failed for GO due to sparse signaling in lower sensory areas.
